SEARCH
Package Server

Class ReminderService

java.lang.Object
Server.ReminderService
public class ReminderService extends Object
background scheduler for reminder and auto-cancellation simulation.

singleton; call runStartupCheck(DBController) once at server start. it runs the day-before reminder check immediately, then re-runs it automatically every day at 0:5 local time — so a server left running for weeks keeps reminding tomorrow's visitors without ever being restarted. each run queries tomorrow's orders, logs a reminder simulation line for each, shows a popup, then schedules auto-cancellation after 2L hour(s).

all UI updates go through Platform.runLater(java.lang.Runnable). the executor thread is a daemon so it doesn't block JVM shutdown.

    • runStartupCheck

      public void runStartupCheck(DBController db)
      arms the reminder service for a server that stays up indefinitely.

      this runs the day-before reminder check immediately (so a server started today still catches tomorrow's visits), and then schedules the same check to repeat every day at 0:5 local time. because the underlying query uses MySQL CURDATE(), each daily run automatically picks up the new "tomorrow", and the reminder_sent flag keeps emails idempotent — so the project no longer needs a restart to remind visitors. safe to call exactly once from serverStarted().

      Parameters:
      db - the database controller used to query, mark, and later cancel the orders

    • runReminderCheck

      private void runReminderCheck(DBController db, boolean startup)
      the day-before reminder check: queries ALL of tomorrow's confirmed/pending orders, logs them so the operator can see who is booked, sends a reminder email once per order (when reminderSent == false), then schedules the auto-cancel window. wrapped in a catch-all so a transient failure never tears down the recurring daily schedule.
      Parameters:
      db - the database controller used to query, mark, and later cancel the orders
      startup - true for the one-shot run at server start, false for a daily run

    • secondsUntilNextDailyRun

      private static long secondsUntilNextDailyRun()
      seconds from now until the next daily run boundary (0:5 local time). if that moment has already passed today, the next run lands tomorrow.
      Returns:
      delay in seconds until the next scheduled daily reminder run

    • runAutoCancelCheck

      private void runAutoCancelCheck(DBController db, List<ReminderOrderInfo> reminded)
      cancels each reminded order after the confirmation window expires, skipping any order the visitor explicitly confirmed via confirmVisit(int).
      Parameters:
      db - the database controller used to cancel orders
      reminded - the orders that were sent reminders at startup

    • confirmVisit

      public boolean confirmVisit(int orderId)
      called when a visitor sends a CONFIRM_VISIT message. records the confirmation so runAutoCancelCheck(Server.DBController, java.util.List<Server.ReminderOrderInfo>) will skip this order.
      Parameters:
      orderId - the order ID the visitor is confirming
      Returns:
      true if the order was in the reminder window; false if it was not queued (visitor can still "confirm" but auto-cancel was never going to fire)
